subject: GalaxyBank compliance recap & artifact asks
messages:
From: Sasha Klein <sasha.klein@galaxybank.com>
To: avery.johnson@redwood.ai
Cc: Howard Liu <howard.liu@galaxybank.com>
Date: Mon, 01 Feb 2027 13:05:00 -0800
Subject: Post-call: Redwood compliance deep-dive recap

Hi Avery —

Thanks again for the call this morning. Quick write-up so we have a shared set of asks and can prioritize internally. High-level pain points we surfaced: 
- SOC 2 scope & evidence gaps: we still need clear artifacts for logging, alerting, and change control tied to the infra that sees customer data.
- Audit logs: sample formats and retention policy; need to confirm what fields are logged (user, actor, timestamp, request/response IDs) and whether logs contain any sensitive payloads.
- Retention & egress controls: GalaxyBank requires 7-year retention for transaction metadata and stricter egress rules for production systems.
- DPA language & data residency: we need a DPA draft that maps to our legal controls and confirms Redwood's export/subprocessor policies.
- Pen test / vulnerability evidence: either a recent executive summary or description of your pen-testing cadence and remediation SLAs.

Next steps we need from Redwood to get procurement moving: 
1) An artifact inventory (what artifacts you can provide: SOC 2 report or SOC 2 letter, pen-test exec summary, sample audit logs, retention policy docs, DPA).
2) Initial artifacts dropped to a secure location or uploaded to our intake portal by Feb 8 (we realize some items will be redacted).
3) Confirmation of who on your side will own the artifact collection + a single point of contact for follow-ups.
4) A proposed timeline for any staging access (read-only) so our security team can validate logs and controls.

We plan to review the artifacts with our InfoSec and Procurement teams the week of Feb 15. Howard and I will be the points for that review.

Appreciate the fast response — sending over the list here so it's explicit.

Regards,
Sasha Klein
Head of Information Security
GalaxyBank

---

From: Avery Johnson <avery.johnson@redwood.ai>
To: Sasha Klein <sasha.klein@galaxybank.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 01 Feb 2027 15:10:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: Redwood compliance deep-dive recap

Hi Sasha —

Great to connect earlier. Thanks for the clear summary — we can meet all of the asks you listed and I've mapped owners below so there's no confusion. Summary of pain points we heard from your side: SOC 2 evidence for logging/change control, sample audit logs and retention mapping, DPA + subprocessor list, and a recent pen-test cadence/executive summary.

Owners / commitments: 
- Artifact inventory & SOC 2 evidence: Marissa Cole (Security & Compliance liaison) — will produce a checklist of available artifacts and expected timelines.
- Audit logging & retention details: Dev Patel (Platform lead) — will provide sample log exports (redacted as needed) and a retention policy doc.
- DPA & legal: me (I will coordinate our legal team and share a DPA draft for redlines).

Immediate next steps from Redwood: 
1) Attached: "redwood-evidence-checklist.xlsx" (artifact inventory template) and "soc2-evidence-mapping.md" (high-level map of common SOC 2 control references to artifacts). Please review and flag anything missing.
2) We'll aim to deposit an initial artifact drop by Feb 8 into a secure shared folder (we will provide a pre-authenticated link or S3 presigned upload).
3) Dev will prepare a sample audit log export (CSV + JSON examples) and retention policy doc by Feb 5.
4) I'll send a DocuSign for the DPA draft once we've included your legal redlines — target to get a signed DPA in early Feb if possible.

Proposed meeting: 30 minutes the week of Feb 15 to review artifacts with your InfoSec — I suggested two time slots in the calendar invite. If you prefer earlier, we can move the review to the week of Feb 8 after the artifact drop.

Attachments: 
- redwood-evidence-checklist.xlsx (attachment)
- soc2-evidence-mapping.md (attachment)

Let me know if that sequencing works. We will mark items with priority flags for the artifacts likely to unblock Procurement (DPA, SOC 2 letter, pen-test exec summary, sample audit logs).

Thanks —
Avery Johnson
Enterprise Sales Manager
Redwood Inference
avery.johnson@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0184

Date: Tue, 02 Feb 2027 09:15:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: Redwood compliance deep-dive recap

Avery —

Thanks — that plan looks good. I'm attaching the DPA template we'll use on our side (galaxybank-dpa-template.docx) and a short audit spec (audit-log-specs.pdf) that outlines the CSV/JSON fields we expect for ingestion. A few clarifications: 
- For the pen-test info, a redacted executive summary is fine — our security reviewers just need scope, date, and remediation cadence (no full reports).
- For SOC 2, if you can provide a SOC 2 Type II attestation or a SOC letter covering relevant controls, that will speed procurement.
- For sample logs, we prefer both CSV and ndjson samples (with redaction).

DocuSign link for a quick signature on our DPA (you can upload your redlines first): https://docusign.com/transactions/AA123456789

I'll also attach our procurement intake form — filled by Howard — so you get context on our internal timelines.

Attachments: 
- galaxybank-dpa-template.docx (attachment)
- audit-log-specs.pdf (attachment)

Best,
Sasha Klein
Head of Information Security
GalaxyBank
